records.title: Magnetic resonance imaging bias field correction improves tumor prognostic evaluation after transcatheter arterial chemoembolization for liver cancer
records.abstract: BACKGROUND Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a key treatment approach for advanced invasive liver cancer (infiltrative hepatocellular carcinoma). However, its therapeutic response can be difficult to evaluate accurately using conventional two-dimensional imaging criteria due to the tumor’s diffuse and multifocal growth pattern. Volumetric imaging, especially enhanced tumor volume (ETV), offers a more comprehensive assessment. Nonetheless, bias field inhomogeneity in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) poses challenges, potentially skewing volumetric measurements and undermining prognostic evaluation. AIM To investigate whether MRI bias field correction enhances the accuracy of volumetric assessment of infiltrative hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE, and to analyze how this improved measurement impacts prognostic prediction. METHODS We retrospectively collected data from 105 patients with invasive liver cancer who underwent TACE treatment at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University from January 2020 to January 2024. The improved N4 bias field correction algorithm was applied to process MRI images, and the ETV before and after treatment was calculated. The ETV measurements before and after correction were compared, and their relationship with patient prognosis was analyzed. A Cox proportional hazards model was used to evaluate prognostic factors, with Martingale residual analysis determining the optimal cutoff value, followed by survival analysis. RESULTS Bias field correction significantly affected ETV measurements, with the corrected baseline ETV mean (505.235 cm³) being significantly lower than before correction (825.632 cm³, P < 0.001). Cox analysis showed that the hazard ratio (HR) for corrected baseline ETV (HR = 1.165, 95%CI: 1.069-1.268) was higher than before correction (HR = 1.063, 95%CI: 1.031-1.095). Using 412 cm³ as the cutoff, the group with baseline ETV < 415 cm³ had a longer median survival time compared to the ≥ 415 cm³ group (18.523 months vs 8.926 months, P < 0.001). The group with an ETV reduction rate ≥ 41% had better prognosis than the < 41% group (17.862 months vs 9.235 months, P = 0.006). Multivariate analysis confirmed that ETV reduction rate (HR = 0.412, P < 0.001), Child-Pugh classification (HR = 0.298, P < 0.001), and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage (HR = 0.578, P = 0.045) were independent prognostic factors. CONCLUSION Volume imaging based on MRI bias field correction can improve the accuracy of evaluating the efficacy of TACE treatment for invasive liver cancer. The corrected ETV and its reduction rate can serve as independent indicators for predicting patient prognosis, providing important reference for developing individualized treatment strategies.

records.title: The role of artificial intelligence and image processing in the diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of liver cancer: a narrative-review
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and image processing are revolutionising the diagnosis and management of liver cancer. Recent advancements showcase AI's ability to analyse medical imaging data, like computed tomography scans and magnetic resonance imaging, accurately detecting and classifying liver cancer lesions for early intervention. Predictive models aid prognosis estimation and recurrence pattern identification, facilitating personalised treatment planning. Image processing techniques enhance data analysis by precise segmentation of liver structures, fusion of information from multiple modalities, and feature extraction for informed decision-making. Despite progress, challenges persist, including the need for standardised datasets and regulatory considerations.

records.title: The contribution of magnetic resonance imaging to radiotherapy treatment planning
records.journal: University of Thessaly Institutional Repository (University of Thessaly)
records.abstract: Radiotherapy constitutes a fundamental therapeutic modality in modern oncology, aiming to deliver a therapeutic radiation dose to the target volume while simultaneously sparing surrounding organs at risk.The accuracy of radiotherapy planning largely depends on the quality of imaging information.Although Computed Tomography (CT) remains the cornerstone of radiotherapy treatment planning as the primary imaging modality for dose calculation, its limited soft-tissue contrast results in significant uncertainties in target delineation. The present study investigates the role and contribution of MagneticResonance Imaging (MRI) in radiotherapy treatment planning.Initially, the fundamental physical principles of MRI are presented, followed by an analysis of advanced techniques such as Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI), functional MRI (fMRI), Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS), and Perfusion MRI.Subsequently, the clinical applications of MRI are examined across various oncological sites, including head and neck tumors, liver malignancies, rectal cancer, prostate cancer, and glioblastomas, with emphasis on improved delineation of target volumes (GTV/CTV) and organs at risk (OARs).Particularemphasis is placed on the prominent role of MRI throughout the entire therapeutic pathway of each malignancy, from diagnosis and radiotherapy planning to treatment response assessment.Furthermore, indicative data regarding thefuture prospects of MRI in MR-Linac-based radiotherapy delivery are briefly presented.The experimental component of this thesis includes a comparative analysis of treatment plans generated with and without MRI integration, demonstrating statistically significant differences in target volumes and safety margins.The findings confirm that incorporating MRI into radiotherapy planning enhances geometric accuracy, reduces uncertainty, and contributes to the delivery of a more personalized and safer radiotherapeutic approach.

records.title: Automated diagnosis and classification of liver cancers using deep learning techniques: a systematic review
records.abstract: Liver cancer is one of the main causes of cancer-related mortality globally. It is a rising threat with over 700,000 deaths and 800,000 new cases annually. To tackle this, deep learning (DL) artificial intelligence (AI) tools have been researched extensively to create predictive models that aid in the early diagnosis and classification of liver cancers. The liver, however, is prone to metastasis from various gastrointestinal cancers, making it difficult to correctly classify tumors present in the organ. This paper is a thorough systematic evaluation of several published studies that used deep learning algorithms to diagnose, classify, and predict common liver tumors, including but not limited to Hepatocellular carcinoma and Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Articles selected in this review have been published between 2016 and 2024 from Google Scholar, Research Gate, Science Direct, IEEE Xplore, Springer Link, and other resources as per the PRISMA guidelines. Amongst these, the highest recorded accuracy was 99.38%, with other studies showing close results at 97% and below. The highest recorded sensitivity was 100%. Selected studies were also analyzed based on their choice of dataset, DL algorithm, and preprocessing techniques. Magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography (CT) are by far the preferred medium for imaging data because of their high resolution; however, CT is used more often because it’s cheaper and provides a better view of extrahepatic space. Genetic datasets showed great potential in differentiating between primary and secondary liver cancers. Nonetheless, several gaps were identified across the current literature. The problem of accurately differentiating cancer types in the liver still persists. However, the use of 3D imaging datasets aids in this significantly. Though, it is clear that 3D datasets are underutilized. Dynamic imaging is also beneficial and should be considered more often. For future research, we strongly recommend the use of Gaussian Mixture Model, Watershed Transform, Sparsity classification, DLIR and Siamese algorithms as they each showed promising results. Lastly, we have shown a benchmark framework for a predictive AI model that can be referred to develop future models. Though numerous past methods have produced excellent prediction results, the prevalence of liver cancer-related deaths has not yet been reduced. To address the difficulties in the field of cancer prediction, more thorough research is required, along with the development of more efficient decision support systems using deep learning.

records.title: Automated segmentation and quantification of histological liver features for MASH/MASLD scoring
records.abstract: Abstract The increasing global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) creates an urgent need for objective histopathological assessment. Conventional histological approaches are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, we propose a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline for the segmentation and characterisation of histological liver features of MASH/MASLD. Segmentation was applied to H&E sections from 45 mice and 44 humans with MASH/MASLD. Our qHisto (quantitative histology) method, is nnU-Net-based and quantifies key histological components of the MASH-score, including steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation and ballooning. Additionally, we determined novel features that are inaccessible through manual histology, like the distribution of fat droplet sizes, nuclear aspect ratio and heatmaps. qHisto parameters showed strong positive correlations with conventional histology scores (fat: R = 0.91, inflammation: R = 0.70, ballooning: R = 0.47) and with hepatic fat fraction by magnetic resonance imaging ( R = 0.87). Our novel scores showed that nuclei deformation is driven by large fat droplets rather than the overall amount of fat. A key advantage of our method is spatially resolved, precise histological quantification to provide detailed assessment of disease severity. By automating time-consuming and repetitive readouts, qHisto improves standardisation and reproducibility of MASH/MASLD feature quantification and provides scalable, slide-wide analysis that supports histopathologists and enhances clinical assessment.

records.title: Predicting complications after hepatectomy for hepatocellular carcinoma: a narrative review focused on liver failure
records.abstract: Hepatectomy is a potentially curative treatment for selected patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but postoperative complications remain an important source of morbidity and mortality. This narrative review focuses on prediction models for post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF), with additional discussion of selected non-PHLF complications. It emphasizes validation design, transportability, calibration, clinical actionability, and the distinction between evidence from HCC cohorts and cohorts with mixed diagnoses. PHLF has the most mature prediction literature because its risk is closely related to measurable liver reserve, portal hypertension, future liver remnant volume and function, and resection extent. Clinical and serum scores are accessible but generally provide moderate discrimination. Volumetric, functional, and imaging assessments add complementary information, whereas machine learning and radiomics models can capture nonlinear and high-dimensional patterns but often rely on small cohorts, random internal splits, and incomplete calibration reporting. Evidence for bile leakage includes validated clinical scores and a large externally validated machine learning model. Models for postoperative ascites, intra-abdominal infection or abscess, and surgical site infection remain sparse and are often perioperative rather than purely preoperative. Across endpoints, high apparent discrimination has not established clinical benefit. Future studies should prioritize standardized endpoints, adequate effective sample size, independent geographic external validation, calibration, net benefit assessment, and risk updating at successive stages. Current models should be used as decision support tools rather than substitutes for multidisciplinary clinical judgment.

records.abstract: PURPOSE: We assessed the safety and efficacy of magnetic resonance (MR)-guided microwave ablation for treating hepatic malignancies. METHODS: This retrospective single-center review evaluated patients who underwent MR-guided microwave ablation for hepatic malignancies between 02/15/2017-04/22/2020. Complications were classified following CIRSE guidelines. Local tumor progression (LTP), local tumor recurrence (LTR), non-target progression (NTP), progression-free survival (PFS) and time to progression (TTP) were assessed, with data presented as mean ± standard deviation. RESULTS: Sixteen patients (60.75 ± 14.4 years; 9 males, 7 females) underwent 17 MR-guided microwave ablation for 21 hepatic malignancies (17 (81.0%) hepatocellular carcinoma, 1 (4.8%) cholangiocarcinoma, 2 (9.5%) metastases, and 1 (4.8%) suspicious lesion in a patient with primary sclerosing cholangitis). Lesion size was 12.2 ± 4.8 mm and total procedure time 138 ± 53 minutes. Complications included fever (N = 2), abdominal pain (N = 2), biloma (N = 1), and reactive cholecystitis (N = 1). These resolved with pain medication for one patient and antibiotics for another. No tumor recurrence was observed at ablation sites (LTP and LTR = 0%) at 36.7 ± 28.2 months. NTP occurred in 11 patients (68.8%) with a TTP of 14.8 ± 11.4 months. PFS was 44 months (95% CI: 10-85 months). Three patients died during follow-up - one from complications after liver transplantation and two from disease progression. Post-ablation liver transplantation was performed in two patients. CONCLUSION: MR-guided microwave ablation for hepatic malignancies is safe and effective, with no local tumor recurrences noted over a follow-up period of 36.7 ± 28.2 months. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: MR-guided microwave ablation is a promising minimally invasive treatment for hepatic malignancies, demonstrating no LTR at 36.7 ± 28.2 months. Precise, radiation-free needle placement in real-time and effective targeting of small tumors may further improve future patient care.

records.title: A Bibliometric and Visualization Analysis of Hydroxyapatite-Supported Fe₃O₄ Nanocomposite and Future Perspective
records.journal: EKSAKTA Journal of Sciences and Data Analysis
records.abstract: Fe₃O₄/Hydroxyapatite (Fe₃O₄/HA) composites have attracted considerable attention for their magnetic recoverability and potential applications in medical and environmental remediation. This bibliometric review examines the research landscape of Fe₃O₄/HA photocatalysts using publications indexed in the Scopus database from 2021 to 2026. Bibliometric analyses were conducted using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny to evaluate publication trends, influential authors, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, and leading publication sources. The results show steady growth in scientific output during the study period, accompanied by expanding international research collaborations. Keyword mapping identified photocatalysis, wastewater treatment, pollutant degradation, adsorption, and environmental remediation as the primary research themes. The Journal of Environmental Chemical Engineering and Materials Today Communications were the most influential publication sources in this field. China emerged as the leading contributor to global research output and collaborative activities, followed by notable contributions from Iran, India, and the Indonesia–Malaysia partnership. The findings demonstrate the continued development of Fe₃O₄/HA-based research and reveal emerging opportunities for advancing sustainable photocatalytic technologies for environmental applications.

records.title: ORC1 expression features and its prognostic significance in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Objective Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Conventional biomarkers alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP) have diagnostic limitations, particularly for early-stage disease. This study investigated the expression profile of ORC1 in HBV-related liver disease and its association with HBV infection, disease progression, and prognosis. Methods 178 participants were recruited: 124 HBV-positive cases (49 HBV-HCC, 33 HBV-cirrhosis, 42 chronic hepatitis B) and 54 HBV-negative controls (35 non-HBV-HCC, 19 hepatic hemangioma). Tissue ORC1 was detected by immunohistochemistry, and serum ORC1 was measured by ELISA in a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum. Logistic regression identified factors associated with high ORC1 expression. ROC curves were used to evaluate the discrimination of tissue ORC1, AFP, and DCP for HBV-HCC, and the correlation between ORC1 and tumor diameter was analyzed. TCGA-LIHC data were used for external validation. Results Tissue ORC1 was significantly upregulated in HBV-positive patients, and HBV infection was independently associated with high ORC1 expression (P<0. 001). ORC1 expression increased progressively from chronic hepatitis B to cirrhosis to HCC. In a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum, tissue and serum ORC1 were moderately correlated (Spearman rs=0. 554, 95% CI 0. 085–0. 822, P = 0. 021). Tissue ORC1 showed moderate discrimination between HBV-HCC and HBV-LC (AUC = 0. 64) and between HBV-HCC and CHB (AUC = 0. 66). ORC1 expression was not significantly associated with tumor diameter ( P >0. 05). High ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC (HR = 1. 7, P = 0. 0026). Conclusion ORC1 upregulation is independently associated with HBV infection and increases with disease progression in HBV-related liver disease. Although tissue ORC1 showed only moderate discrimination for HBV-HCC, high ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC. These findings suggest that ORC1 is primarily a proliferation- and progression-related marker in HBV-related liver disease.

records.title: Comprehensive motion management for liver SBRT on a 1.5 T MR-Linac: Initial clinical experience and dosimetric comparison with an ITV-based workflow
records.abstract: Background and purpose Respiratory-gated MR-guided workflows enable expiration-gated liver stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) based on real-time intrafraction target monitoring. We evaluated the dosimetric impact and early clinical feasibility of this approach by comparing clinically delivered expiration-gated plans with retrospectively generated non-gated ITV-based plans. Methods The first 20 consecutive patients treated with online adaptive MR-guided SBRT for primary or secondary liver malignancies on a 1.5 T MR-Linac between October 2024 and April 2025 were included. Five patients had two lesions, treated with separate plans in two patients, resulting in 22 matched plan pairs. For each clinically delivered gated plan, a retrospective ITV-based plan with identical prescription dose was generated. Paired differences were tested with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and p -values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. The dose–volume analysis was considered exploratory. Results Median planning target volume was lower with the gated workflow than with ITV-based planning (28.0 vs. 41.9 cc). Organ-at-risk constraint violations were fewer with the gated workflow (10 vs. 19), with 11 violations resolved and 2 newly occurring. PTV D98% did not differ significantly ( p = 0.41), although one gated and four ITV-based plans showed PTV D98% < 95%. Uninvolved liver dose was significantly lower with the gated workflow (median Dmean difference 0.97 Gy and 0.93 Gy for three- and five-fraction plans; adjusted p ≤ 0.037). Among 93 evaluable fractions, the mean plan-level median active delivery time was 7.6 min for three-fraction and 6.7 min for five-fraction treatments. Conclusion Expiration-gated MR-guided liver SBRT reduced target volumes and improved normal tissue sparing without compromising target coverage or routine clinical feasibility.

records.title: Primary Malignant Neoplasms of the Liver
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the sixth most common cancer worldwide and the third most common cause of cancer death. Characteristic imaging features, that is, arterial phase hyperenhancement and delayed washout, on contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or multiphase computed tomography scan, can yield a noninvasive diagnosis of HCC in most patients, although biopsy is needed in some cases. Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a neoplasm of the epithelium of the intra- or extrahepatic biliary tree. Risk factors and mechanisms underlying the development of intra versus extrahepatic CCA differ, and this chapter focuses on intrahepatic CCA. Almost all possible types of sarcoma have been reported as primary liver tumours. These include embryonal sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, and so on. A standardized management of these lesions is not available, partly because of the rarity of these lesions but also because they are aggressive tumours with a very poor prognosis.

records.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
records.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

records.title: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines for pediatric hepatoblastoma: a systematic review and expert recommendations from Korea
records.abstract: Hepatoblastoma (HB) is the most common primary liver malignancy in children, predominantly affecting those younger than 3 years of age. Although the overall survival rate has improved significantly over the past few decades, standardized clinical practice guidelines for HB in Korea have been lacking. This clinical practice guideline was developed to provide evidence-based recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of HB in children. A multidisciplinary working group comprising pediatric hematologists/oncologists, radiologists, surgeons, pathologists, and methodologists systematically reviewed the literature published up to May 2023. For pretreatment imaging, both abdominal computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are useful for PRE-Treatment EXTent of disease (PRETEXT) staging, with each modality offering distinct advantages. PRETEXT staging at diagnosis is recommended as it provides valuable prognostic information. For standard-risk HB (PRETEXT I-III without metastasis and alpha-fetoprotein ≥100 ng/mL), cisplatinbased chemotherapy without doxorubicin is recommended over cisplatin-doxorubicin combination therapy, as it demonstrates equivalent survival outcomes with fewer adverse effects. In carefully selected patients who are eligible for complete resection at diagnosis, upfront surgery without neoadjuvant chemotherapy should be considered to spare unnecessary chemotherapy and its toxicities. For patients with residual pulmonary metastases after chemotherapy, pulmonary metastasectomy should be considered. Sodium thiosulfate administration following cisplatin should be considered to reduce ototoxicity, although the supporting evidence is derived predominantly from standard-risk patients and its availability in Korea remains limited. Regarding histological subtypes, well-differentiated fetal HB is associated with favorable outcomes and may be treated with surgery alone, whereas the small cell undifferentiated pattern is no longer classified as a HB subtype and requires immunohistochemical and molecular testing to distinguish it from malignant rhabdoid tumor and other small round cell tumors. This guideline represents the first evidence-based clinical practice guideline for pediatric HB in Korea. It aims to standardize the diagnostic and therapeutic approaches, ultimately improving outcomes for Korean children with HB. Given the rarity of this tumor, international collaboration and prospective data collection remain essential for future guideline updates.

records.title: Glypican-3-targeted pH-responsive dual-drug co-loaded nanoliposomes for precision combined chemotherapy and anti-metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) chemotherapy is limited by poor drug selectivity, severe systemic toxicity, and frequent drug resistance. This study aimed to construct a novel pH-responsive nanoliposome system co-loaded with paclitaxel (PTX) and doxorubicin (ADR), functionalized with anti-glypican-3 (GPC3) antibodies, for precision combined chemotherapy and anti-metastasis of HCC. Methods: PTX-loaded nanoliposomes were first prepared via reverse evaporation, followed by co-loading with ADR and bovine serum albumin to form PTX-ADR-BNP. GPC3 antibodies were conjugated onto the surface to obtain GPC3-PTX-ADR-BNP. The system was evaluated for particle size, zeta potential, encapsulation efficiency, and pH-responsive release. Cytotoxicity was assessed against HCC and normal cells. In vivo antitumor efficacy, biosafety, and anti-metastatic effects were evaluated using subcutaneous xenograft and lung metastasis models. Results: GPC3-PTX-ADR-BNP exhibited uniform particle size (~180 nm), high encapsulation efficiencies (>96% for PTX, >95% for ADR), and pH-responsive release (~80% at pH 5.3 within 16 h, slow release at pH 7.4). In vitro, it showed potent cytotoxicity against MHCC97H and HuH-7 cells (half-maximal inhibitory concentration: 41.21 and 54.19 μg/mL) with minimal toxicity to normal cells. In vivo, the system prolonged plasma half-life, enhanced tumor accumulation, and achieved >59% tumor inhibition. Biosafety assessments, including hemolysis (<1% at all tested concentrations), serum biochemistry, hematological parameters, and histopathological examination of major organs, showed no significant toxicity compared to the control group. In the pulmonary metastasis model, it effectively suppressed lung metastasis, outperforming free drug and non-targeted groups. Conclusion: GPC3-PTX-ADR-BNP integrates GPC3-mediated active targeting with pH-responsive release for efficient anti-tumor and anti-metastatic effects, with high biocompatibility and low toxicity, offering a promising strategy for precision HCC therapy.

records.title: A Controlled Generative Model for Segmentation of Liver Tumors
records.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generative model representing the formation of liver CT images and employ it for segmentation of hepatic tumors. We extend the graphical model used in label fusion techniques for the segmentation of multi-modality Magnetic Resonance brain images. To resemble atlas data, we segment the first slice by a physician and propagate it for processing of subsequent slices. We include a knowledge-based constraint in the model that is considered as a key difference with classical generative models. We compared our method with conventional Bayesian techniques and state-of-the-art hepatic tumor segmentation algorithms. We achieved a measure of 0.86 ± 0.06 and 0.76 ± 0.09 regarding Dice and Jaccard metrics respectively that is better than recent researches.

records.title: Automatic segmentation and classification of the liver tumor using deep learning algorithms
records.journal: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)
records.abstract: Liver tumors are one of the life-threatening cancers with the fastest-growth rates worldwide. Early detection of tumors may therefore reduce morbidity and increase the survival rate. The development of automated techniques for the precise segmentation of hepatic tumors is essential for assisting doctors in tumor diagnosis and preoperative planning for surgical treatment of the liver which reduces the risk of surgical resection. The classification and segmentation of hepatic tumors in Computerized Tomography (CT) scan pose a great challenge due to noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, and variability in tumor tissue appearance, shape, size, and location. In this study, we describe a novel method for automatic segmentation and classification of hepatic tumors in CT scan images using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks. For tumor segmentation, we created a modified Dense U-net model. The classification framework is based on a novel deep CNN with a pre-trained VGG-16 network to distinguish between normal and malignant liver tumors. The proposed system was evaluated based on MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge dataset and obtained the best result with a Dice Score of 95.40%, Jaccard Index of 92%, and accuracy of 92.60% for segmentation and the classification model has achieved an accuracy of 96%, Sensitivity of 95.80%, Specificity of 96.20% and Precision of 95.80%.

records.title: Automatic liver tumor segmentation from CT scans with knowledge-based constraints
records.abstract: Automatic hepatic tumor segmentation is a crucial step for diagnosis and surgery planning. This paper presents a new fully automatic technique to segment the tumors in liver structure with no interaction from user. Contrast enhancement is applied to the slices of segmented liver, then adding each image to itself to have a white image with some pepper noise and tumors as dark gray spots. After applying Gaussian smoothing, Isodata is used to threshold the tumor in the slice. In order to eliminate erroneous segmentation, discriminative rule based on diagnostic knowledge on liver cancer shape is applied along with a 3-D consistency check is performed based on three-dimensional information that a lesion mass cannot appear in a single slice independently. Tests are performed on 9 abdominal datasets and promising result shows that sensitivity and specificity for automatic liver tumor segmentation are 87% and 99% respectively.

records.title: Comparison of two‐dimensional and three‐dimensional iterative watershed segmentation methods in hepatic tumor volumetrics
records.abstract: In this work the authors compare the accuracy of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) implementations of a computer-aided image segmentation method to that of physician observers (using manual outlining) for volume measurements of liver tumors visualized with diagnostic contrast-enhanced and PET/CT-based non-contrast-enhanced (PET-CT) CT scans. The method assessed is a hybridization of the watershed method using observer-set markers with a gradient vector flow approach. This method is known as the iterative watershed segmentation (IWS) method. Initial assessments are performed using software phantoms that model a range of tumor shapes, noise levels, and noise qualities. IWS is then applied to CT image sets of patients with identified hepatic tumors and compared to the physicians' manual outlines on the same tumors. The repeatability of the physicians' measurements is also assessed. IWS utilizes multiple levels of segmentation performed with the use of "fuzzy regions" that could be considered part of a selected tumor. In phantom studies, the outermost volume outline for level 1 (called level 1_1 consisting of inner region plus fuzzy region) was generally the most accurate. For in vivo studies, the level 1_1 and the second outermost outline for level 2 (called level 2_2 consisting of inner region plus two fuzzy regions) typically had the smallest percent error values when compared to physician observer volume estimates. Our data indicate that allowing the operator to choose the "best result" level iteration outline from all generated outlines would likely give the more accurate volume for a given tumor rather than automatically choosing a particular level iteration outline. The preliminary in vivo results indicate that 2D-IWS is likely to be more accurate than 3D-IWS in relation to the observer volume estimates.

records.title: Procesamiento de imágenes médicas mediante conjuntos neutrosóficos
records.abstract: El procesamiento de imágenes médicas constituye un área crítica para el diagnóstico, donde la incertidumbre y la ambigüedad inherentes a los datos biomédicos limitan la efectividad de los métodos convencionales. En este contexto, la teoría neutrosófica ha emergido como un marco matemático robusto para el manejo explícito de información imprecisa. Este artículo de revisión presenta un análisis del estado del arte en procesamiento de imágenes médicas mediante conjuntos neutrosóficos, abarcando sus fundamentos teóricos, las principales técnicas de preprocesamiento, segmentación y extracción de características, y su integración con modelos de inteligencia artificial y aprendizaje profundo. Asimismo, se examinan comparativamente sus ventajas frente a los métodos clásicos basados en lógica difusa, así como sus limitaciones actuales relacionadas con la escalabilidad, la automatización y la integración en flujos clínicos digitales. Finalmente, se discuten los retos y oportunidades futuras, destacando el potencial de la neutrosofía híbrida y explicable como herramienta clave para el desarrollo de sistemas médicos más precisos, interpretables y confiables en la medicina de precisión contemporánea.

records.title: Advances in Deep Learning and Image Processing for Brain Tumor Detection and Classification: A Comprehensive Review
records.journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
records.abstract: Brain tumor identification and classification by the application of deep learning and sophisticated image-processing techniques have been receiving a lot of attention in the medical field. Accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient outcome rely on the accurate identification and differentiation of brain tumors, such as gliomas, meningiomas, and metastases. The most recent developments in deep learning-based techniques for brain tumor identification and categorization by applying medical imaging data, including Computed Tomography (CT). This study looks at CT and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). The main topic of this study is the general theory and developments in deep learning methods for the identification and classification of brain tumors. It investigates how the precision and efficacy of tumor detection can be increased through a variety of models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The paper emphasizes the Significance of applying novel deep-learning techniques for facilitating precise and automated brain tumor identification for individualized treatment, with an emphasis on important achievements, challenges, and opportunities in the area.

records.title: Robots for CT-guided needle insertion: clinical implementation and future perspectives
records.abstract: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

records.title: Comprehensive motion management for liver SBRT on a 1.5 T MR-Linac: Initial clinical experience and dosimetric comparison with an ITV-based workflow
records.abstract: Background and purpose Respiratory-gated MR-guided workflows enable expiration-gated liver stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) based on real-time intrafraction target monitoring. We evaluated the dosimetric impact and early clinical feasibility of this approach by comparing clinically delivered expiration-gated plans with retrospectively generated non-gated ITV-based plans. Methods The first 20 consecutive patients treated with online adaptive MR-guided SBRT for primary or secondary liver malignancies on a 1.5 T MR-Linac between October 2024 and April 2025 were included. Five patients had two lesions, treated with separate plans in two patients, resulting in 22 matched plan pairs. For each clinically delivered gated plan, a retrospective ITV-based plan with identical prescription dose was generated. Paired differences were tested with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and p -values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. The dose–volume analysis was considered exploratory. Results Median planning target volume was lower with the gated workflow than with ITV-based planning (28.0 vs. 41.9 cc). Organ-at-risk constraint violations were fewer with the gated workflow (10 vs. 19), with 11 violations resolved and 2 newly occurring. PTV D98% did not differ significantly ( p = 0.41), although one gated and four ITV-based plans showed PTV D98% < 95%. Uninvolved liver dose was significantly lower with the gated workflow (median Dmean difference 0.97 Gy and 0.93 Gy for three- and five-fraction plans; adjusted p ≤ 0.037). Among 93 evaluable fractions, the mean plan-level median active delivery time was 7.6 min for three-fraction and 6.7 min for five-fraction treatments. Conclusion Expiration-gated MR-guided liver SBRT reduced target volumes and improved normal tissue sparing without compromising target coverage or routine clinical feasibility.

records.title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): An Itch Receptor Drives Melanoma
records.abstract: Mas-Related GPCR X4 (MRGPRX4) is a sensory neuron-restricted receptor for cholestatic itch. Here, we identify MRGPRX4 as an unexpected melanoma driver. MRGPRX4 is upregulated in melanoma and is confined to invasive, neural-crest-like and pre-EMT states associated with dedifferentiation and therapy resistance. Ectopic MRGPRX4 expression in mouse melanocytes drives 100% penetrant, highly metastatic melanoma, demonstrating oncogenic behavior. MRGPRX4 promotes melanoma cell proliferation and invasion through basal, ligand-independent, PI3K-AKT-MAPK activation. Multi-omics links MRGPRX4 expression to a mesenchymal/neural-crest–like program that defines a distinct invasive MRGPRX4+ niche. Comparing transcptomics of MRGPRX4-driven tumors shows a broad overlap with BRAF/NRAS-driven tumors; however, the MRGPRX4 model also enriches an ECM-rich, invasive neural crest–like melanoma state. MRGPRX4 further remodels the tumor microenvironment toward an immunosuppressive, checkpoint-high state enriched in suppressive myeloid cells. Pharmacologic MRGPRX4 inhibition suppresses basal signaling and limits melanoma growth and invasion. In sum, melanoma exploits MRGPRX4 to acquire an invasive and immunosuppressive phenotype, nominating this somatosensory GPCR as a promising therapeutic target.

records.title: Reviewer #1 (Public review): An Itch Receptor Drives Melanoma
records.abstract: Mas-Related GPCR X4 (MRGPRX4) is a sensory neuron-restricted receptor for cholestatic itch. Here, we identify MRGPRX4 as an unexpected melanoma driver. MRGPRX4 is upregulated in melanoma and is confined to invasive, neural-crest-like and pre-EMT states associated with dedifferentiation and therapy resistance. Ectopic MRGPRX4 expression in mouse melanocytes drives 100% penetrant, highly metastatic melanoma, demonstrating oncogenic behavior. MRGPRX4 promotes melanoma cell proliferation and invasion through basal, ligand-independent, PI3K-AKT-MAPK activation. Multi-omics links MRGPRX4 expression to a mesenchymal/neural-crest–like program that defines a distinct invasive MRGPRX4+ niche. Comparing transcptomics of MRGPRX4-driven tumors shows a broad overlap with BRAF/NRAS-driven tumors; however, the MRGPRX4 model also enriches an ECM-rich, invasive neural crest–like melanoma state. MRGPRX4 further remodels the tumor microenvironment toward an immunosuppressive, checkpoint-high state enriched in suppressive myeloid cells. Pharmacologic MRGPRX4 inhibition suppresses basal signaling and limits melanoma growth and invasion. In sum, melanoma exploits MRGPRX4 to acquire an invasive and immunosuppressive phenotype, nominating this somatosensory GPCR as a promising therapeutic target.

records.title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
records.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
records.abstract: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

records.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
records.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.
